question: What will Rosstat's preliminary estimate of Russia's Q3 2026 GDP growth (year-on-year) be?

calls.reasoning: MinEk's monthly-indicator estimate for Q3 2026 is +0.6% y/y (Jul 0.6, Aug 0.8, Sep 0.5), published 28 Oct 2026. Rosstat preliminary prints have deviated from the MinEk quarterly figure by +0.1 (Q1'26), ~+0.4 (Q2'26), ~0 (Q2/Q3'25), ~-0.3 (Q1'25): slight upward mean, SD ~0.3. Upside: Zabotkin said Q3 grows faster than H1 (0.6); Sep industrial production +1.8%; Q2 upside surprise. Downside: agriculture -12.3% in Sep (Q3 -3.9%), mining -4.1%, CBR research says growth 'very restrained', CBR Aug expectation 0.5. No prediction market found on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold. Median ~0.6-0.65.
calls.dossier:
- MinEk 'O tekushchei situatsii' (28 Oct 2026, Kommersant/RIA/Prime): Q3 2026 GDP +0.6% y/y; Jan-Sep +0.6%; monthly Jul +0.6, Aug +0.8, Sep +0.5.
- MinEk Sep sector detail (Kommersant 28 Oct 2026): base industries +0.7% (Aug +0.9); agriculture -12.3% y/y in Sep after +6.6% Aug, Q3 agriculture -3.9%; mining -4.1% (Aug -1.3%); wholesale -1.9% (Aug -0.5%); freight turnover +2.2% (Aug +4.2%); manufacturing recovering.
- Industrial production Jul +0.4, Aug -0.6, Sep +1.8 y/y (question background).
- CBR (5 Aug 2026, Interfax): expected Q3 2026 +0.5% y/y after Q2 0.8% (its own Q2 estimate); cited temporary capacity losses.
- CBR research bulletin 'What trends say' (14 Oct 2026, Prime): growth in Q3 continued 'at a very restrained pace overall for GDP'; domestic demand slowed less than output. No number given.
- Zabotkin (9 Oct 2026, background): Q3 growth faster than H1 (H1 = +0.6%), trough likely passed.
- HSE consensus (Aug 2026): Q3 +0.6%.
- Track record of Rosstat preliminary minus MinEk quarterly estimate: Q1 2026 -0.2 vs MinEk -0.3 (CBR -0.5) => +0.1; Q2 2026 1.3 vs MinEk 0.9 / CBR 0.8 => +0.4; Q3 2025 Rosstat 0.6 vs MinEk ~0.6 => ~0; Q2 2025 ~1.1 vs ~1.1 => ~0; Q1 2025 1.4 vs MinEk ~1.7 => ~-0.3 (2025 figures from memory). Base: Q3 2025 = +0.6%.
- Resolution: resolves off Rosstat 'Spravka o predvaritelnoi otsenke dinamiki VVP v III kvartale 2026' (13 Nov 2026), index minus 100, one decimal; not MinEk or CBR estimates, and not the December 'pervaya otsenka'.
- Event window: single release 13 Nov 2026 (or first Rosstat doc on/after 12 Nov); as of 2 Nov 2026 the quarter's data are complete and only publication remains.
- Searched without finding: a numeric CBR Q3 nowcast from Oct 2026; analysts' polls for Rosstat Q3 print; any prediction market (Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold: none found).
calls.reference_class: Rosstat preliminary quarterly GDP y/y prints vs the MinEk monthly-based quarterly estimate published ~2 weeks earlier, 2025-2026

calls.reasoning: Anchor: MinEk's monthly-indicator estimate for Q3 2026 is +0.6% y/y. Rosstat preliminary prints have tracked MinEk with a recent upward lean (+0.1 in Q1'26, +0.4 in Q2'26, ~0 in Q3'25). Zabotkin said Q3 grew faster than H1 (0.6). September industrial production was +1.8%. Downside: Q3 agriculture -3.9%, mining down, and a CBR July projection of 0.5% with October commentary calling growth 'very restrained'. Median 0.7, roughly symmetric, SD ~0.35. No prediction market found on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold (per the runs and the harness search).
calls.reconciliation: All three runs report the same facts: MinEk Q3 +0.6% (Jul 0.6/Aug 0.8/Sep 0.5), Q3 agriculture -3.9%, mining -4.1% in Sep, CBR's August Q3 expectation of 0.5%, and Rosstat-minus-MinEk gaps of +0.1 (Q1'26) and +0.4 (Q2'26). The 2025 gaps are partly from memory and unverified; Run 1 recalls Q1'25 at about -0.3. I could not check these without web access, so they are kept as uncertain, which leaves the mean bias at roughly +0.1 to +0.15. The only real dispute is a judgment: median 0.6 (Run 1) vs 0.7 (Runs 2 and 3). I take 0.7 on the recent upward lean plus Zabotkin's 'faster than H1' remark, and keep the tails wide because of the harvest shock. I keep Run 3's slightly wider dispersion.

disagreements.claim: Median should be 0.6 (anchored to MinEk) vs 0.7 (recent Rosstat upward bias)
disagreements.verdict: Took 0.7: two recent upside gaps plus Zabotkin's comment; agriculture weakness limits further upside
